national_posture.statement: The latest available United States IMSR was still the August 5 0730 MDT edition at cutoff; it placed the nation at Preparedness Level 5 and listed 94 uncontained large fires, 133 active incidents, and 28,700 assigned personnel.
national_posture.level_meaning: national resources are fully committed, active geographic areas may need emergency measures, and potential for additional significant fires is high

national_posture.statement: CWFIS listed 674 active fires, 4,529 fires year to date, and 9,537,743 acres (3,859,788 hectares) burned year to date for August 6; the latest available CIFFC report was still dated August 5 and placed Canada at National Preparedness Level 5 and British Columbia at agency preparedness level 5, with extreme national resource demand and international resources mobilizing.
national_posture.level_meaning: national demand is extreme, Canadian resources are fully committed, and international resources are being mobilized to sustain operations

incidents.name: Old Trails Fire
incidents.location: West of Spokane near Airway Heights

evacuation.description: Evacuations and road, trail, and area closures remained in effect around the fire.

incidents.operational_outlook: The controlling incident page described moderate flanking and backing, persistent heat in structure debris, continued structure protection and mop-up, and little to no expected perimeter growth before warmer and drier conditions.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage combines the arson case and survivor accounts with community fundraising and a newer, complex-wide estimate of more than 800 structures lost; that newer total is not allocated to individual fires and does not replace the latest official incident-specific IMSR counts.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 48 items from 33 title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours; the seven-day query hit the 100-item display cap, so the 14.3-item daily baseline is a lower bound and the 3.4-times acceleration is an upper bound. High is an editorial override for an unmistakable national headline because the capped baseline prevents proving the three-times threshold; no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Source reconciliation:** The later InciWeb basic-information panel showed 3,574 acres and 5% containment, superseding the highlighted morning update's 3,621 acres and 13%; the report uses the later controlling values. ([InciWeb](https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/wanes-spokane-area-fires)) **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The IMSR's 570 losses are unspecified structures, so they should not be converted into a dwelling count without parcel-level assessment. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Bradley Creek Fire
incidents.location: Okanagan Indian Band reserve near Vernon

evacuation.description: Okanagan Indian Band members were evacuated with very short lead time as the fire entered the reserve community.

incidents.operational_outlook: BC Wildfire Service continued to classify Bradley Creek FSR as out of control and showed four evacuation orders and three evacuation alerts from the Okanagan Indian Band and neighboring jurisdictions.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage continues to center on the preliminary estimate of about 230 homes destroyed in the Okanagan Indian Band community while shifting toward the ongoing out-of-control response, displaced residents, and community support.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 40 items from 24 title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours versus 88 items in the seven-day query, a 12.6-item daily baseline and 3.2-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Source reconciliation:** CIFFC's August 5 priority table now lists Bradley Creek separately at 2,852 hectares, matching the exact BCWS K41351 page. ([BC Wildfire Service](https://wildfiresituation.nrs.gov.bc.ca/incidents?fireYear=2026&incidentNumber=K41351); [CIFFC](https://ciffc.net/situation/)) **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The roughly 230-home estimate is the strongest new residential-loss signal in Canada today, but it remains a preliminary estimate from the Okanagan Indian Band chief rather than a completed parcel-level damage assessment. ([Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/wildfire-canada-homes-destroyed-british-columbia-fbbb7f027adb04a9c9b47a109de74082))
critical_alert_reasons: at least 25 newly damaged or destroyed structures
named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Autumn Lane Fire
incidents.location: Spokane and Stevens counties near Suncrest and Nine Mile Falls

evacuation.description: Evacuations and road and trail closures remained in effect, including Level 3 zones around Suncrest and Nine Mile Falls.

incidents.operational_outlook: The controlling incident page described moderate fire behavior and continuing aggressive structure protection in the wildland-urban interface, with critically dry fuels expected to remain active after the morning inversion lifted.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage emphasizes persistent hot spots, ongoing structure protection, and continuing evacuation constraints even as the later official page held containment at 13%.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 38 items from 25 title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours versus 98 items in the seven-day query, a 14.0-item daily baseline and 2.7-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The 80 losses are an unspecified-structure total, while the continued threat is explicitly residential; keep realized loss and residential exposure as separate fields. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Fairview Fire

evacuation.description: Evacuations and road, trail, and area closures remained in effect near Mead.

incidents.operational_outlook: The controlling incident page described moderate backing, creeping, and smoldering, persistent heat in structure debris, continued structure protection and mop-up, and little to no expected perimeter growth.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage treats Fairview as part of the wider Spokane disaster and reports complex-wide containment and loss developments; no new Fairview-specific loss allocation was published.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 24 items from 18 title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours versus 81 items in the seven-day query, an 11.6-item daily baseline and 2.1-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Source reconciliation:** The later InciWeb basic-information panel showed 992 acres and 13% containment, superseding the highlighted morning update's 1,056 acres and 5%; the report uses the later controlling values. ([InciWeb](https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/wanes-spokane-area-fires)) **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The 57 losses are unspecified structures and the infrastructure threat is qualitative, so neither should be converted into a residential count or modeled exposure count. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Aspen Acres Fire

evacuation.description: Area and road closures remained in effect; the IMSR did not report an active evacuation count.

incidents.operational_outlook: A local Type 3 organization had assumed command; the official page continued to show 101,961 acres and 71% containment with minimal expected fire behavior and ongoing closure and repair work.

attention.coverage_summary: Recent coverage emphasizes the transfer to a local incident team and recovery activity; one roundup described a slight containment dip, while the later controlling InciWeb page remained at 71%.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 19 items from nine title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours versus 79 items in the seven-day query, an 11.3-item daily baseline and 1.7-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** Treat the IMSR's 915 lost structures as a cumulative incident total, not an August 5 damage increment; the report does not split the total into residences, commercial buildings, or outbuildings. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))

incidents.name: Kaiser Canyon Fire
incidents.controlling_agency: Bureau of Indian Affairs and Alaska Incident Management Team 2

evacuation.description: Evacuations and road and area closures remained in effect south of Nespelem.

incidents.operational_outlook: The controlling incident page described active fire behavior and continued structure protection around Nespelem, Agency, Disautel, Highway 155, and the Highway 21 corridor under a warming and drying trend.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage emphasizes Kaiser Canyon as Washington's largest active fire, continued evacuations and structure protection, and persistent hot, dry conditions.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 18 items from 12 title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours versus 54 items in the seven-day query, a 7.7-item daily baseline and 2.3-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Source reconciliation:** The later InciWeb basic-information panel showed 136,887 acres and 43% containment, while the highlighted morning update and August 5 IMSR showed 136,713 acres and 48%; the report uses the later controlling values. ([InciWeb](https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/wacoa-kaiser-canyon); [NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf)) **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The 44 losses are cumulative and unspecified by occupancy class; numerous structures were still threatened, but the IMSR gave no numerical exposure count.
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Pear Lake Fire
incidents.location: Thompson-Nicola Regional District and Village of Clinton

evacuation.description: BC Wildfire Service showed eight active evacuation orders issued by regional districts, First Nations, and the Village of Clinton, plus four evacuation alerts.

incidents.operational_outlook: The fire remained out of control with eight evacuation orders and four alerts; recent coverage reported extreme behavior on the northwest flank and incoming Mexican reinforcements, while damage assessment remained incomplete.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage has shifted from initial loss assessment toward extreme fire behavior on the northwest flank, international reinforcement, and the continued threat around Clinton; the reported 120 affected properties still should not be read as 120 destroyed dwellings.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 14 items from 12 title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours versus 61 items in the seven-day query, an 8.7-item daily baseline and 1.6-times acceleration; no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** Do not equate about 120 affected properties with 120 destroyed dwellings: the regional district said some properties lost only garages, sheds, or other outbuildings while the residences remained standing, and assessment was incomplete. ([CTV News](https://www.ctvnews.ca/vancouver/article/more-than-100-structures-lost-in-bcs-pear-lake-wildfire-officials-say/))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Rowe Creek Complex
incidents.location: South of Fossil across central Oregon counties
incidents.controlling_agency: Pacific Northwest Complex Incident Management Team 3 and Oregon State Fire Marshal

evacuation.description: The official update directed residents to county evacuation maps because zones could change quickly; it did not state a single complex-wide evacuation level.

incidents.operational_outlook: Structural crews continued point protection and triage near developed areas while U.S. Highway 26 remained closed for suppression operations.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage emphasizes the complex's exceptional scale, improving containment, and a public meeting; recent headlines cited about 329,000 acres and 62%, while the later InciWeb basic-information panel had grown to 340,276 acres at the same containment.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 25 items from 19 title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours; the seven-day query hit the 100-item display cap, so the 14.3-item daily baseline is a lower bound and the 1.7-times acceleration is an upper bound. Because the 1.5-times threshold cannot be established from the censored baseline, attention is conservatively Low; no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Source reconciliation:** The later InciWeb basic-information panel showed 340,276 acres and 62% containment, while the highlighted update cited 329,012 acres and 62% and the August 5 IMSR showed 325,265 acres and 57%; the report uses the latest controlling basic-information values. ([InciWeb](https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/orprd-rowe-creek-complex); [NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf)) **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The complex-wide 25-loss total is not classified by occupancy, and current updates do not establish a new loss increment.

global_overview.statement: The reviewed international headline sample remained concentrated in Europe: France and Spain retained the largest reported structural and evacuation consequences, Greece shifted from active response toward return and animal recovery, and Albania still had recent evacuation headlines; no Australian event reached the same headline threshold at the cutoff. This is a headline scan, not comprehensive worldwide operational intelligence.

global_events.name: Mallakastër and Gjirokastër fires
global_events.status: Ground and aerial crews were actively protecting homes in Mallakastër; a second likely lightning-caused fire remained active in mountainous terrain south of Gjirokastër
global_events.evacuations: About 15 families were evacuated with livestock and pets.
global_events.summary: The Albania events were the newest promoted international fires at the cutoff, but no verified structure-loss or burned-area count was published in the reviewed report.

global_events.name: Megara and western Attica fires
global_events.status: Remaining containment lines near Athens were lifted Wednesday as residents returned, while recovery groups worked to reunite displaced animals
global_events.structure_loss_description: Dozens of homes were reported torched; an exact destroyed-home count was not reported.
global_events.evacuations: Multiple evacuations were ordered during the fire; no consolidated count was reported in the latest reviewed article.
global_events.summary: The fire burned more than 24,711 acres (10,000 hectares), and volunteers reported rescuing more than 280 animals; those counts describe area and animal recovery, not structural loss.

global_events.name: Bordeaux–Le Porge fire
global_events.status: The fire was contained and thousands of evacuees were returning, but it was not fully extinguished
global_events.evacuations: More than 224,000 people fled during France's largest civilian evacuation outside wartime.
global_events.summary: Fire damage exposed more than 400 suspected World War II shells and other munitions in Le Porge, adding an unusual recovery and access constraint.

global_events.name: Almería fire and central Spain fire complexes
global_events.status: Many July fires were easing or controlled, but recurrent heatwaves were sustaining renewed wildfire risk
global_events.evacuations: More than 1,500 people evacuated during the Almería fire; later fires also displaced residents around Madrid.
global_events.summary: The merged fires near Madrid were estimated at about 172,974–197,684 acres (70,000–80,000 hectares), while a campsite operator reported that about half of its mobile homes burned; no consolidated national structure-loss total was available.

rejected_candidates.name: Sinlahekin Fire
rejected_candidates.reason: The IMSR reported rapid growth and two structures lost, but no numeric threatened-structure count; it remained below today's eight-incident structural-impact cutoff.

rejected_candidates.name: Modrite Fire
rejected_candidates.reason: The IMSR reported 15 structures lost, 35% containment, evacuations, and qualitative threats, but it remained below the 25-structure promotion threshold and lacked a higher structural signal.

rejected_candidates.name: Bench Fire
rejected_candidates.reason: The IMSR reported 13 structures lost and 84% containment; it remained below the 25-structure promotion threshold and showed substantially greater suppression progress than promoted fires.

rejected_candidates.name: Fox Fire
rejected_candidates.reason: The IMSR reported eight structures lost and 61% containment, below the structural-impact cutoff for the displayed watchlist.

rejected_candidates.name: Second Flat Fire
rejected_candidates.reason: The IMSR reported seven structures lost and 55% containment, below the structural-impact cutoff for the displayed watchlist.

rejected_candidates.name: Ainslie Creek and Brunswick Creek fires
rejected_candidates.reason: CIFFC listed both as out-of-control British Columbia priority fires, but reviewed sources did not establish qualifying structural loss, a numeric structure threat, or headline momentum comparable with Bradley Creek and Pear Lake.
